page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with 5669 GB of local NVMe SSD, while no dedicated GPUs are present.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ds_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance in multi-threaded operations and database workloads. It achieves top-tier status in Passmark CPU scores, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 596.61 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations perform at 156.15 million operations per second. The server also excels in static web serving throughput at 151.5 GB/sec and shows strong memory bandwidth, reaching 348.8 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads. Large language model inference benchmarks show top-tier prompt processing speeds for both 7B and 70B models, though text generation speeds fall into the average to strong ranges.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D96ds_v7 offers high resource density by combining a massive 96-vCPU compute allocation with a substantial 5669 GB local NVMe SSD. This eliminates the need for separate premium storage attachments for high-I/O workloads, optimizing the hardware-to-resource profile. The server is highly suited for enterprise database hosting, high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data decompression, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
